name: Toll transponder interoperability: which pass works in which states
description: For each US toll transponder programme (E-ZPass, SunPass and SunPass PRO, TxTag and the Central US partners, and the rest as their pages prove reachable): the states and networks where that transponder is accepted, from the operating agency's own interoperability page with a verbatim quote. No authority maintains the national matrix — the E-ZPass Group's member list sits behind an agency login, and the only assembled versions are toll-calculator vendors' blog posts. The answers cross-cut: SunPass PRO works on E-ZPass roads in 19 states but the plain SunPass Mini works in only six; a TxTag works in Kansas and Oklahoma but not on E-ZPass roads; Florida's Turnpike accepts E-ZPass but only via specific transponder models. Answers 'will my E-ZPass work in Florida', 'which toll pass should I get for a Texas-to-Chicago drive', and 'does SunPass work in Georgia'. One record per transponder-programme statement of acceptance, quoting the agency page.

records.accepted_in: Texas, Kansas, Oklahoma, Colorado and most toll roads in Florida
records.source_quote: The <https://www.centralustolling.com/> Central United States Interoperability Partners (CUSIOP) allow drivers to use toll roads in Texas, Kansas, Oklahoma, Colorado and most toll roads in Florida with a single toll account. Drivers must have an active toll tag issued by the Texas Department of Transportation (TxTag), Harris County Toll Road Authority (EZ TAG), North Texas Tollway Authority (TollTag), Kansas Turnpike Authority (KTAG), Oklahoma Turnpike Authority (PIKEPASS), Colorado E-470 Public Highway Authority (ExpressToll), or Florida Department of Transportation (SunPass) installed in their vehicle.
